name: Multilingual Prompting (Hindi, Hinglish)
question: Will the prompt work when users write in Hindi or Hinglish?
summary: Prompts and structured outputs for users who write in Hindi, Hinglish in Roman script, or another Indian language. Keep JSON keys and enum labels in English while values may be in any language, say explicitly which language and script to reply in, normalise spoken amounts and dates (“saadhe teen hazaar” → 3500), and include a code-mixed example or two. Measure accuracy per language slice, not only overall.
useCases: Support bots and assistants for Indian customers
Extraction of intents, amounts and dates from chat messages
Any prompt first written and tested only in English

items.detail: labels stay stable whatever the input language
“reply in the user’s language and script” written into the prompt
spoken or mixed amounts to digits in rupees
one or two Hinglish and Hindi examples, not only English
accuracy for English, Hinglish and Hindi separately
Devanagari often takes more tokens than Roman text; measure it

steps: Keep keys and enum labels in English, values in any language
Tell the model which language and script to reply in
Add rules and examples for amounts, dates and names in code-mixed text
Evaluate each language slice and fix the weakest first
pitfalls: Translating every message to English first and losing names and amounts
Enum labels that come back in Hindi and break the schema
Reporting one overall accuracy that hides a weak Hinglish slice
remember: English labels, the user’s language in replies, and test every slice.
caption: Illustrative: Kaveri Bank, a fictional bank, extracts intents and amounts from 1,000 messages in English, Hinglish and Hindi.

code.text: SYSTEM = """Extract the ticket as JSON. Keys and intent labels stay in English.
Reply in the same language and script as the customer:
Hinglish in Roman letters gets Hinglish, Hindi in Devanagari gets Devanagari.
Amounts: convert words to digits in rupees.
Example: "mera card block karo, kho gaya"
"reply": "Aapka card abhi block kar diya gaya hai."}"""

steps.title: Keep keys and labels in English
steps.text: The schema fixes the keys and the four intent labels. Whatever the customer writes, “refund_status” comes back spelled the same way, so the JSON validates.

steps.title: Say which language to reply in
steps.text: Without this line about one Hindi or Hinglish reply in five came back in English. Stating the language and the script fixes almost all of them.

steps.title: Normalise amounts
steps.text: Customers write “saadhe teen hazaar”, “3.5k” or “₹3,500”. A short rule with examples turns them all into 3500.

steps.title: Show a code-mixed example
steps.text: One Hinglish example teaches the pattern better than any English example. Hinglish intent accuracy rises from 78% to 90%.

steps.title: Test each language separately
steps.text: English at 95% can hide Hinglish at 78%. Report accuracy for every slice.

steps.title: Fix the weakest slice first
steps.text: Add examples and rules where the slice is weakest, then re-run all slices so English does not regress.

pros: Outputs validate whatever language the user writes in
Replies match the customer’s language and script
Amounts and dates are captured reliably from code-mixed text
Per-slice tests reveal the users you are failing
cons: Examples in several languages lengthen the prompt
Devanagari text can cost more tokens
Needs labelled test data per language
Rules for numbers and dates need upkeep
avoidWhen: All users write in one language and the output is free text
A translation service is required anyway for audit copies (translate the output, not the input)

practice.scenario: Kaveri Bank, a fictional bank, reads support messages in English, Hinglish and Hindi. The prompt keeps JSON keys and the intent labels in English, tells the model to reply in the customer's language and script, converts spoken amounts such as “saadhe teen hazaar” to 3500, and shows one Hinglish and one Hindi example. Accuracy is reported for each language separately.

industries.use: Balance, refund and card-block requests typed in Hinglish

library.name: OpenAI Python SDK
library.what: Structured outputs: responses.parse with a Pydantic model fixes keys and enum values.

practice.note: The model name is a placeholder; any API with JSON-schema outputs works the same way.

samples.code:
from typing import Literal
from openai import OpenAI
from pydantic import BaseModel

client = OpenAI()

class Ticket(BaseModel):
    intent: Literal["refund_status", "block_card", "kyc_update", "other"]
    amount_inr: int | None
    reply_lang: Literal["en", "hi-Deva", "hi-Latn"]
    reply: str

SYSTEM = """Extract the ticket. Keys and intent labels stay in English.
Reply in the customer's language and script.
Convert amounts to digits in rupees: "saadhe teen hazaar" = 3500, "dedh lakh" = 150000.
Example: "mera card kho gaya, block karo" -> block_card, reply_lang hi-Latn."""

for msg in ["bhai 3500 ka refund kab aayega?", "मेरा कार्ड ब्लॉक कर दो"]:
    t = client.responses.parse(model="gpt-5-mini", instructions=SYSTEM,
                               input=msg, text_format=Ticket).output_parsed
    print(t.intent, t.amount_inr, t.reply_lang, t.reply)

numericDrill.question: 400 English messages score 95%, 300 Hinglish 90% and 300 Hindi 92% on intent. What is the overall accuracy, in percent?

interview.question: How do you design an extraction prompt for Hinglish users?
interview.answer: Keep keys and enum labels in English, state the reply language and script, add rules and examples for amounts and dates, include code-mixed examples, and report accuracy per language slice.

interview.question: Should you translate user messages to English before the model?
interview.answer: Usually not: modern models read Hindi and Hinglish directly, and translation can mangle names, amounts and intent. Translate outputs when an English audit copy is needed.

mistakes.mistake: Enum labels allowed in any language
mistakes.fix: Fix labels in English with a schema
Report English, Hinglish and Hindi separately

quiz.question: Why keep intent labels in English when users write in Hindi?
options: Labels stay stable, so the JSON validates and code can rely on them
Hindi cannot be stored in JSON
quiz.explanation: Stable labels matter to downstream code, whatever the input language.

quiz.question: What should a prompt say about reply language?
options: Reply in the customer’s language and script
quiz.explanation: Stating language and script avoids English replies to Hinglish users.

quiz.question: “saadhe teen hazaar” should become which amount?
quiz.explanation: Saadhe teen hazaar means three and a half thousand.

quiz.question: “dedh lakh” is how many rupees?
quiz.explanation: Dedh lakh is one and a half lakh: 1,50,000.

quiz.question: Which improve a prompt for code-mixed users? Select all that apply.
options: Translating every message to English first
quiz.explanation: Pre-translation can mangle names and amounts.

quiz.question: Overall accuracy is 93% but Hinglish is 79%. What is the problem with reporting only 93%?
options: It hides the users you are failing

quiz.question: English 95% on 400, Hinglish 90% on 300, Hindi 92% on 300. Overall?
A reply to a Hinglish message comes back in Devanagari. What was missing?
quiz.explanation: Say language and script: Hinglish in Roman letters.

quiz.question: Where is translation useful in a multilingual pipeline?
options: Translating outputs when an English or Hindi copy is needed
quiz.explanation: Translate outputs for audit or other teams, not inputs by default.

quiz.question: Which belong in a multilingual test set? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: Test every language and pattern your users write in.

quiz.question: Code-mixed examples add 350 tokens to each of 1,00,000 daily messages. How many extra tokens a day?
Why can Devanagari text cost more than Roman text?
options: Tokenizers often split Devanagari into more tokens
It uses more bytes on disk only
quiz.explanation: Many tokenizers produce more tokens for Indic scripts; measure yours.

quiz.question: The model returns intent "रिफंड स्थिति". What fixes this for good?
options: A schema with English enum values
quiz.explanation: A schema enforces the allowed labels.

quiz.question: Adding Hinglish examples raised Hinglish to 90%. What next?
options: Re-run every slice to check English did not drop

quiz.question: A customer writes "recharge 299 wala plan chahiye". Intent?
Which are good normalisation rules? Select all that apply.
Users write in Tamil too. What is the minimum change?
options: Add Tamil to the reply rule, a Tamil example and a Tamil test slice
quiz.explanation: Each language needs examples and a test slice.

quiz.question: "refund kab aayega" is in which script?
quiz.explanation: Hindi words written in Roman letters.

quiz.question: Intent accuracy on Hinglish rose from 78% to 90% on 300 messages. How many more are right?
Which is the best first step when a multilingual bot underperforms?
options: Measure accuracy per language to find the weak slice
quiz.explanation: Find where it fails before changing things.
